extracted.intended_audience: companies and financial institutions (sustainability teams, ESG leads) preparing or submitting science-based GHG emission reduction targets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/validation criteria for companies (including SMEs and financial institutions) to develop, submit, validate, communicate and maintain science-based greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction and net-zero targets with the SBTi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of science-based targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Science-based targets give companies a clearly-defined path to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in line with limiting global warming to 1.5°C. They define how much and how quickly a business must reduce its emissions to be in line with the Paris Agreement goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SBTi's Foundations of Science-based Target Setting paper and Corporate Net-Zero Standard for underlying rationale and technical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBTi Services validation role
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi Services is the distinct target validation entity. Organizations develop science-based targets using the Science Based Targets initiative’s standards and guidance, then submit them to SBTi Services for validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If targets conform they are validated and published as 'Targets set.' If not in conformance, SBTi Services provides feedback to support resubmission. Register via the SBTi Services Validation Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GHG Protocol accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi closely aligns with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol as the foundation for GHG accounting and target-setting methodologies and uses its standards and guidance to ensure consistent, accurate and credible emissions measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to GHG Protocol Corporate Standard for scope definitions and accounting; also use Scope 2 Guidance and Scope 3 Guidance for details on each scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emissions scope coverage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Science-based targets must cover scopes 1 and 2. For companies whose scope 3 emissions cover more than 40% of their combined scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, targets must cover scope 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the SBTi Criteria Assessment Indicators for full detail on scope coverage rules and how to assess the 40% threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory inclusion of emissions for validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBTi requires companies to provide 100% of their GHG emissions for validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may exclude up to 5% of scope 1 and scope 2 emissions combined, and may exclude a maximum of 5% of scope 3 emissions from the total scope 3 inventory. At least 67% of the total reported and excluded mandatory scope 3 emissions must be covered under target(s). Exclusions must be quantified and reported. 'Negligible' or unavailable data are not valid reasons for not reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base year selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Base year must be representative, verifiable and have accurate scope 1, 2 (and where relevant, scope 3) emissions data; base year must be no earlier than 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unusual years (e.g., pandemic, major M&A) that are not business as usual. Companies submitting targets for validation in 2025 must submit inventory data for 2023 at the earliest. Use SBTi resources to help pick an appropriate base year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target year timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Near-term targets must have a target year of 5–10 years from the date the target is submitted to the SBTi. Long-term targets must have a target year of 2050 or before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only targets submitted in the first half of a calendar year can include the current year in the threshold. Example windows for 2024 and 2025 submission periods are provided in the guidance—companies are encouraged to choose more ambitious (earlier) target years than the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred ambition (temperature alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi strongly encourages companies to commit to the highest level of ambition by setting a net-zero, 1.5°C-aligned target across their value chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies that committed on/after 15 July 2022 are required to use criteria that require alignment with 1.5°C for most companies. Existing SBTs set under previous criteria may remain valid until due for update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of target-setting approach
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two approaches for setting scope 1 and 2 targets: sector-based approach and absolute-based approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should not default to the easiest target but use the most ambitious decarbonization scenarios and methods that lead to earliest reductions and least cumulative emissions. Alignment with latest SBTi criteria is advised to avoid multiple updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods available for setting scope 3 targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may set near-term scope 3 targets using: absolute contraction (1.5°C or well-below 2°C), Sectoral Decarbonization Approach (SDA) (1.5°C or well-below 2°C), supplier/customer engagement targets, economic intensity targets, or physical intensity targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More details are included in the SBTi Criteria Assessment Indicators and the new version of the criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-step process for setting science-based targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should follow: 1) Register (Validation Portal), 2) Commit (optional letter of intent), 3) Develop targets with SBTi standards/guidance, 4) Submit target forms for validation, 5) Communicate (announce target), 6) Disclose (annual progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMEs have a tailored process. See Standard Operating Procedure for the Validation of SBTi Targets and Getting Started Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME validation route eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the SME validation route, SMEs must meet all of: have <10,000 tCO2e across scope 1 and location-based scope 2; are not classified in Financial Institutions or Oil & Gas sectors; are not required to set sector-specific criteria (except certain FLAG entities); are not a subsidiary whose parent’s combined businesses fall into the corporate validation route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, three or more of the following must be true: employ <250; turnover <€50m; total assets <€25m; are not in a mandatory FLAG sector. Eligibility is confirmed during registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME target options and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: SME validation route target options include near-term targets (absolute scope 1 and 2 reductions by 2030), near-term maintenance targets for SMEs with zero scope 1/2, and net-zero targets (absolute reductions in scope 1, 2, and 3 by 2050 or before).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net-zero targets must be complemented by near-term targets aligned to 1.5°C. SMEs without scope 1/2 emissions can use maintenance option but must provide documentation explaining '0' emissions and strategies to maintain them. SME net-zero targets require scope 3 coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME recalculation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: SME targets shall be recalculated and revalidated when significant changes occur (e.g., changes in eligibility for SME route, consolidation approach, significant changes to emissions or company structure, adjustments to data/methodologies resulting in significant base year changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a significance threshold of 5% or less: a 5% change in total base year emissions triggers base year recalculation; a 5%+ change in base year emissions covered within a target boundary triggers target recalculation. Follow SME Criteria Assessment Indicators NT C27 for full triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLAG target requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must set FLAG (Forest, Land and Agriculture) science-based targets if they either: i) have land-intensive activities in FLAG-designated sectors (e.g., forestry, agricultural production, animal source, food processing, retailing, tobacco), or ii) have FLAG-related emissions that total 20% or more of overall emissions across scopes 1, 2 and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FLAG targets must be submitted along with other targets via SBTi Services (cannot be submitted individually). Companies with existing validated targets must submit a Near Term Update + FLAG target. See FLAG Guidance and FLAG sector page for timelines and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fossil fuel / oil & gas sector policy and eligibility categories
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi paused commitments and validations from the fossil fuel sector until an oil & gas method is finalized. Companies with any level of direct involvement in exploration, extraction, mining and/or production of oil, natural gas, coal or other fossil fuels (category 1) cannot commit; certain companies with limited revenue from fossil fuel activities (category 2) may join under specified thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category 2 examples: companies deriving <50% revenue from sale/transmission/distribution of fossil fuels or providing equipment/services to fossil fuel companies; companies with <5% revenue from fossil fuel extraction assets; certain electric utilities. Subsidiaries considered case-by-case; SBTi may remove companies post-evaluation. Policy reviewed regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of fossil-fuel-related sold-products emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Near-Term C22, companies involved in sale, transmission or distribution of natural gas and/or other fossil fuel products must set near-term and long-term scope 3 targets for the 'use of sold products' category that are at minimum consistent with 1.5°C decarbonization, irrespective of the emissions share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer engagement targets (C19) are not eligible for this criterion. See C23 for guidance on the 50% revenue threshold and contact OGsector@sciencebasedtargets.org for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on automakers (land transport)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automaker target validations were temporarily paused (March 2022) and the pause was lifted on 20 March 2024 with publication of Land Transport Guidance which provides a new method aligning automakers' use-phase (scope 3 category 11) with 1.5°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automakers with commitments expiring up to six months from release of Land Transport Guidance must submit targets within six months. Validated automaker targets remain valid for five years from approval but are encouraged to increase ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on counting carbon credits toward target progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of carbon credits must not be counted as emission reductions toward the progress of companies’ near- or long-term science-based targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must set targets based on emission reductions through direct action within their own boundaries or their value chains. For market-based accounting approaches, see SBTi guidance on accounting and target achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoided emissions not accepted for target-setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoided emissions fall under a separate accounting system and therefore do not play a role in emission reduction target‑setting or achievement with the SBTi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets are based on corporate inventory accounting (GHG Protocol); avoided emissions cannot be used to justify target ambition or progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon removal / CCS / DAC treatment and neutralization
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon capture and storage/use (CCS/CCU) and direct air capture (DAC) are treated differently: CCU/CCS is typically applied at an emissions source and DAC is currently considered Beyond Value Chain Mitigation (BVCM). Carbon storage applications are not yet fully covered by greenhouse gas accounting methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain carbon removal/storage technologies may be eligible to count towards neutralization requirements under the Corporate Net-Zero Standard (V1.2) and draft V2; consult those standards for neutralization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target review and mandatory five-year update
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are required to review their targets at least every five years from the date of initial validation or last full update across scopes 1, 2, and 3. If targets no longer meet current Criteria, they must be updated and revalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review process: trigger date is end of month five years after validation; companies have six months to complete review and submit evidence to SBTi Services. If update needed, revised targets must be submitted within 12 months of the trigger date. See Mandatory Five-Year Review Guidance and relevant Criteria (NT-C26, NZ-C32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base year / target recalculation procedure and 5% significance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: If changes (e.g., acquisitions, divestments, mergers, methodological adjustments) represent 5% or more of base year emissions, companies must recalculate base year emissions and assess whether targets remain in line with SBTi criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) assess if change ≥5%; (2) recalculate base year emissions per GHG Protocol (fixed base year or rolling base year methods described by GHG Protocol; SBTi does not allow rolling base years for targets); (3) review existing targets for affected alignment; (4) if targets still meet criteria no formal update needed (unless base year changes), otherwise submit target update and book revalidation subject to latest criteria. Companies should provide clear evidence when selecting a new base year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, Reporting & Verification (MRV) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi is introducing an enhanced MRV framework in Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2 to increase transparency and accountability and support assessment of progress against voluntary corporate climate targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the interim, companies should report company-wide GHG emissions and progress through annual/sustainability reports, company websites, and/or disclosure via CDP. See Annex D of Corporate Net-Zero Standard for reporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool development and third-party tool usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party tools can be developed using SBTi resources, but SBTi does not help develop, review, endorse or certify any third-party tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools should use publicly available SBTi resources and be reviewed at least every three months for continued alignment. Developers may not use the SBTi logo or claim endorsement/certification without permission. If a submitted target matches a tool output but falls short of SBTi ambition, validation team may deem the tool output erroneous and request target adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and logo use
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies with validated science-based targets can use SBTi branding (logo and Net-Zero Standard mark) only in accordance with SBTi communications guidance; companies with commitments but not validated targets cannot use the logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logo/branding must be used only in content with a clear reference to the target (e.g., include full target wording alongside the logo or make it easily accessible via a link or footnote). Exceptions apply for certain past Business Ambition for 1.5°C campaign commitments; for other inquiries contact communications@sciencebasedtargets.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure on the Target Dashboard
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi publishes company and target information on its Target Dashboard. Certain company fields are published after commitment and additional fields after target approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a commitment is made the dashboard publishes: company name, ISIN, LEI, headquartered region/location, sector, commitment type, status, deadline, reason for extension/removal, publication date. After target approval it adds: full target language, target type/scopes/base year/target year/value, company temperature alignment, and target publication date. The Target Dashboard updates weekly on Thursdays (usually by 12:00 GMT, no later than 17:30 GMT) and pauses publication near end-of-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of confidential submission data
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi treats commercially sensitive data received from companies as confidential and therefore does not publish all data submitted for validation on the public Target Dashboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential handling enables more detailed information to be reviewed by SBTi Services to provide an accurate assessment of a company’s science-based target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of calendar or fiscal years
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies and financial institutions may set science-based targets using calendar or fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure target-year windows and submission date rules (first/second half of calendar year rules) are applied appropriately relative to chosen year type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excel compatibility and tool output caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: SBTi cannot guarantee support for legacy versions of Microsoft Excel and recommends using the latest version for spreadsheet-based target-setting tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted targets match tool outputs but fall short of SBTi ambition, the Validation Team may deem the tool output erroneous; tool output does not override target assessment criteria and may lead to requested target adjustments.
